eva: quick heads-up — ran a 30m stress run on the canary branch, and we got a repeatable OOM waterfall when the kernel selector flipped from gelu-opt -> generic under long-seq bursts. KV prefill windows spike right before the crash. attaching rough flame + heap snapshot link: https://perf.internal/reports/4298 :alert:
jae: ugh. did the traces show large memcpy or workspace reallocation around the flip?
rachel: yes, saw a ~120ms stall for workspace resize and then a cascade of evictions. stack shows `allocator::grow_workspace()` + `kernel_switch()` repeated.
ev a: exact snippet from nvprof timeline (trimmed):
```
[00:01:23.112] kernel_select: gelu-opt (small seq)
[00:01:23.232] batcher: merged -> seqlen change -> choose generic
[00:01:23.354] allocator: free-run fail -> enlarge workspace(64MB -> 96MB)
[00:01:23.476] kv-cache: demote 18 slots -> eviction debounce
[00:01:23.596] OOM
```
sam: so kernel switching is causing fragmentation and then prefill tries to allocate contiguous chunk and fails. Have you repro'd with prefill disabled?
eva: with prefill disabled the OOM doesn't happen, but tail latency spikes. So prefill is the culprit when combined with aggressive kernel switching and thin per-request caps.
jae: interesting — earlier experiments assumed prefill allocations were small and reusable. This shows fragmentation + resizing makes them non-reclaimable quickly.
rachel: proposal: two levers — (1) make kernel selection prefer 'workspace-stable' variants unless latency benefit > X, (2) add adaptive per-request soft caps that scale with recent seqlen hist.
sam: + add compact-on-evict pass for allocator when fragmentation crosses threshold. cheap compaction could avoid resize.
perf-bot: perf trace summary uploaded: https://perf.internal/artifacts/4298/flame.svg — notable hotspots: memcpy (27%), allocate_zeroed (19%), kv-demote (12%).
eva: quick config prototype I ran locally (YAML) — non-final but reproducible:
```
allocator:
  max_workspace_mb: 512
  compaction_threshold_pct: 18
  allow_inplace_realloc: false
kernel_policy:
  workspace_stable_bias: 0.7   # 0..1, prefer kernels that reuse workspace
  latency_headroom_ms: 6
prefill:
  enabled: true
  soft_cap_per_request_mb: "adaptive" # scale by p95_seqlen
  min_lazy_threshold_tokens: 16
```
jae: how does adaptive cap derive p95? sliding window of 60s? 5min?
rachel: I used 2min sliding + exponential decay. felt responsive without being noisy. results: 40% fewer evictions, 12% tail latency increase but no OOMs.
sam: can we simulate worst-case burst with a synthetic qps/seqlen mix? share the runner config.
eva: runner command I used:
```
./tools/bench --qps 320 --seq-dist "mix: 80% 32, 20% 512" --kernel-swap-prob 0.2 --prefill 1 --duration 1800 --trace-out out/4298
```
je: i mean jae :) will run a stricter reproducer with `--kernel-swap-prob 0.5` and report.
rachel: one more weird note — kernel selector sometimes chooses larger-kernel that uses fewer kernels overall (less switching) but allocates more peak workspace per request. might be worth a cost function: prefer stable-kernel even if slightly higher per-request peak if it saves fragmentation-induced rescales.
sam: agree. also add a cheap countermeasure: when prefill sees recent allocator resize in the last 1s, switch to lazy prefill for the next N requests.
perf-bot: CI perf regression check: candidate branch shows +0.6% median, +9% p99 for long-seq under synthetic load. Baseline is master.
eva: actionable TODOs from thread:
  - jae: run high-swap reproducer and attach full trace (due EOD PST)
  - rachel: prototype kernel selection cost fn (workspace-stability vs latency) and a config knob
  - sam: implement compact-on-evict heuristic + small compaction pass
  - perf-bot: run 2min sliding window perf job on canary and smoke test prefill lazy toggle
please ping if blocked. tagging @jae @rachel @sam :slightly_smiling_face:
jae: ack, starting reproducer now.
rachel: ack, will push a PoC branch tomorrow.
sam: I'll sketch allocator compaction PR and drop notes in PR description.
